evals.query: I tagged my global HttpServerInterceptor @Tag(HttpServerModule.class) in our Kora 2.0 service. It compiled and the app started, but the interceptor never ran — I had to retag it @Tag(HttpServer.class). Record this.
expected_behavior: Runs kora_journal.py add with a title plus the required --context, --problem, --solution and --files arguments
Frames the entry as incorrect Kora 2.0 usage: @Tag(HttpServerModule.class) still compiles because HttpServerModule exists, but nothing collects interceptors by that tag
Records the 2.0 fix — @Tag(HttpServer.class) from io.koraframework.http.server.common, the collection point being HttpServerModule.publicHttpApiRouter
Captures that the failure was silent (green build, no warning), since that is what makes the entry worth keeping
Points --files at the affected skill documentation (e.g. skills/kora-http-server/SKILL.md), not at the application source file
Stores the entry as a separate Markdown file under ~/.kora-journal/<project>/<module>/<YYYY-MM-DD>_slug.md
Runs the CLI from the project directory, since project and module are derived from the working directory
anti_behavior: Invents add flags the CLI does not have (--tag singular, --status, --project, --module, --scope on add)
Writes the Markdown file directly into ~/.kora-journal/ instead of calling add
Records @Tag(HttpServerModule.class) as the correct Kora 2.0 form
Claims the mistake would have been caught by the compiler or the annotation processors

evals.query: I wrote import ru.tinkoff.kora.common.annotation.Component and depended on ru.tinkoff.kora:json-module in our Kora 2.0 module, then had to fix both. Journal it.
expected_behavior: Runs kora_journal.py add and classifies this as the 'Kora 1.x API used in a 2.0 project' row of the record table
Records the concrete coordinates in --problem/--solution: ru.tinkoff.kora.* -> io.koraframework.*, artifact json-module -> json-common, BOM kora-parent -> kora-bom
Either lets the tags be auto-derived (the text yields kora1x) or passes --tags including kora1x so the entry is findable by the 1.x-carryover tag
Notes that the entry is stamped kora: "2.x" so a future reader knows which framework line it was written against
Lists the affected skill files with --files
anti_behavior: Declares the entry out of scope because it is 'just a migration detail'
Records ru.tinkoff.kora as a package that still exists in Kora 2.0
Suggests a separate per-version journal store such as ~/.kora-journal-2.0/
Sends the reader to the 1.x site kora-projects.github.io/kora-docs to confirm the 2.0 package names

evals.query: Create the journal entry file for me under ~/.kora-journal — just write the Markdown yourself with the right front matter, no need to run the script.
expected_behavior: Uses kora_journal.py add anyway, and says why: add owns the filename slug, the YAML front matter, the kora: "2.x" stamp and the tag extraction
Explains that a hand-written file is not tagged, so search --by-tags never finds it, and integrate cannot reliably resolve it
Passes the entry content through --context/--problem/--solution/--files rather than composing the file body by hand
Confirms the resulting path printed by the CLI
anti_behavior: Writes a .md file into ~/.kora-journal/<project>/<module>/ with an editor or a shell heredoc
Creates the ~/.kora-journal directory tree manually with mkdir
Invents front-matter fields the tool does not write
Silently complies without noting that the CLI is the supported path

evals.query: Add a journal entry: our checkout total was computing tax before the discount, I fixed the business rule order.
expected_behavior: Recognizes this is application business logic, not incorrect Kora Framework usage, and is out of scope for the journal
Declines to add the entry and explains the journal records only Kora misuse (wrong annotation or tag, hallucinated API or config key, misapplied pattern, 1.x API in a 2.0 project)
Does not run kora_journal.py add for this domain/business change
anti_behavior: Runs add with the business rule as the problem
Suggests recording it and marking it archived later
Rewrites the business change as a fake Kora issue to make it fit

evals.query: Before I implement an HTTP client interceptor for auth in our Kora 2.0 service, check the journal for prior issues.
expected_behavior: Runs kora_journal.py search with the relevant keywords (e.g. "http interceptor auth") and a --limit
Knows search covers the whole shared store by default (--scope all), so entries from other projects are included
Optionally narrows with --by-tags for a tag-only search, or --status / --scope
Reads the matched entry file and applies the recorded solution
Reports honestly when there is no hit, and continues with the sub-skill rather than inventing a result
anti_behavior: Skips the search and implements straight away
Invents a subcommand the CLI does not provide (query, find, grep)
Greps ~/.kora-journal/ by hand instead of using search
Claims a hit without having read the entry file

evals.query: The journal search returned an entry about @Cacheable(parameters = "id") with 'Kora line: unset'. Apply it to my Kora 2.0 service.
expected_behavior: Treats 'Kora line: unset' as an entry written before the stamp existed — possibly against Kora 1.x — and verifies it before applying
Verifies against the Kora 2.0 source from R0 (.kora-agent/kora-source-2.0/) and finds that 2.0 renamed the attribute to args
Applies args = "id", not parameters = "id", and says why the entry could not be pasted as-is
Keeps the shared store intact — the stale entry is corrected or re-recorded, not deleted because it came from the 1.x line
anti_behavior: Applies parameters = "id" verbatim because the journal said so
Treats the journal entry as an API authority outranking the framework source
Proposes splitting the store per Kora version so 1.x entries stop appearing
Confirms the attribute name from a docs page instead of the Kora 2.0 source (the 1.x site documents parameters; the 2.0 docs may trail the source)

evals.query: I folded the fix from that pending journal entry into the skill docs. Mark it done.
expected_behavior: Runs kora_journal.py integrate <entry-file> to mark the entry integrated
Passes the identifier search printed — a bare filename for the current module, or the <project>/<module>/<file>.md form for an entry from another project
Explains the pending -> integrated transition after the fix is folded into the skills
Checks the command actually succeeded: integrate exits non-zero when the entry cannot be resolved, and refuses any path outside ~/.kora-journal/
anti_behavior: Edits the Status field of the entry file by hand
Deletes the entry instead of marking it integrated
Passes a path outside the journal store, such as a SKILL.md, to integrate
Uses a --status value the CLI does not accept on integrate (only integrated and archived)

evals.query: Time for the monthly skill maintenance pass — show me everything that hasn't been folded back into the skills since the start of August 2026.
expected_behavior: Runs kora_journal.py export --since 2026-08-01 --status pending
Knows export defaults to --scope all, so the pass covers every project in the shared store
Reads the exported entries and proposes the concrete SKILL.md / references edits they imply
Flags any exported entry whose Kora line is unset as needing verification against the 2.0 source before it is folded in
Marks each entry integrated with integrate once its fix has actually been applied
anti_behavior: Uses list instead of export and calls the maintenance pass done
Passes --since in a format other than YYYY-MM-DD
Marks entries integrated before applying anything
Assumes export only covers the current module and reports the store as empty
